## Where things stand after this pass

Real forward motion this round, plus I caught two more compile bugs before they'd have failed a fifth build-verification run.

**The persistence blocker (three fixes in a row now, but each one was a genuinely different bug):** Codex A fixed `RecallSchemaV1.versionIdentifier` to be a `Schema.Version` instead of a `String` — that's what build verification actually flagged this round, and it's correct. I re-checked the whole file against Apple's real `VersionedSchema`/`ModelContainer` API and it now looks right end-to-end: proper `Schema.Version`, `Schema(versionedSchema:)` bridging into `ModelContainer(for:migrationPlan:)`. I still can't run an actual simulator build in this sandbox to confirm — that's the real test next round.

**Two new compile bugs I found and fixed in Codex B's new CSV round-trip test file:**
1. It called `.count`, `.enumerated()`, and `.map()` directly on the result of `CSVParser.parseImportRowsWithDetails(...)` — but that returns `CSVParseResult`, a plain struct with a `.rows` array property, not a `Sequence`. None of those calls would have compiled. Fixed by routing through `.rows`.
2. Two of the three tests compared arrays of tuples with `XCTAssertEqual` (`[(front: String, back: String, note: String?)]`) — Swift tuples can't conform to `Equatable`, so arrays of them can't either, even though the tuple `==` operator itself exists. Fixed by introducing a small private `RoundTripCard: Equatable` struct for the comparisons instead.

Also cleaned up: the two remaining raw `.font(.system(size:))` literals in `StateStateViews.swift` (flagged last round, unaddressed since) now use the existing `DS.Font.iconLarge` token, and a stale doc comment in `SettingsRootView.swift` still claiming reminders was a placeholder screen.

**What's actually working now:** Reminders has real permission handling, an honest toggle, and a working time picker (Codex B + my own `reminders.timePicker` addition last round) — genuinely reachable, nothing fake, clearly documented that it's local-storage-only until a scheduler exists. Stats has a real, well-scoped state model (loading/empty/sparse/loaded) with correct nil-vs-zero retention handling and no fabricated charts. Gap & Limitations remains fully live. CSV now has both fixture-based and round-trip test coverage, and both compile clean after this pass's fixes.

**What's still missing, and I want to be blunt about this since it's now four waves running:** there is still no SM-2 engine anywhere in this repo. That's the project's explicit #1 priority, and three iterations' worth of work has gone into stats/CSV/reminders/persistence scaffolding around a core that doesn't exist yet. There's also still no `DeckRepository`/`CardRepository`/`ReviewRepository`, so the solid UI layer built two waves ago (`DeckListView`, `DeckEditorView`, `CardEditorView`) remains completely unreachable. And Gemini's fallback has now narrated a `ReminderService`/`ReminderScheduler` implementation for a **fourth consecutive iteration** without writing a single file to disk — meanwhile the real reminders UI that Codex B and I actually built has made that narrated code redundant even if it ever did land (same bugs repeated each time: struct instead of the frozen protocol, hardcoded due count, empty `DateComponents()`). That lane isn't producing; it shouldn't keep being assigned reminder-scheduling work on the assumption it will.

CONSENSUS: NO

Next iteration, by lane:
- **data_domain**: SM-2 engine in `RecallScheduling`, full stop — this is overdue and everything else is waiting on it, directly or as a trust signal for the whole app. `ReviewRepository` is the natural follow-on.
- **services_utilities**: `DeckRepository`/`CardRepository` against the now-real, now-likely-compiling `Deck`/`Card` models — this is what turns three waves of built-but-unreachable Study UI into an actual feature. If capacity allows, `ReminderScheduler` too, since Gemini's lane isn't delivering it.
- **primary_ui**: wire `StudyRootView` to `DeckListView`/`DeckEditorView`/`CardEditorView` the moment `DeckRepository` lands; hold on anything review/session-related until `SM2Engine` + `ReviewRepository` exist.
- **polish_resilience**: reminders/stats screens are in good shape now — Demo Data placeholder and force-quit/stale-ID test scaffolding (still needs a real session to test against, but the harness can be prepped) are reasonable next targets.
